| KQ25 | A counter credits a targeted rejection/kill only with the subject's declared verdict and a completed relevant run; an error remains visible and non-passing. A genuine-verdict positive control prevents an always-error classifier from passing. A frozen finite error population names every cell and its oracle before measurement. | Exit1/negative returncode alone earns kill credit; a target FAIL literal before selftest abort earns a kill; errors vanish from the denominator; a sampled suite is described as exhaustive. A fail-closed gate's subject failure is not by itself a mutation kill. | `lessons/round-19-verifier-spotcheck.md` items5/7; `lessons/round-20.md` M1/M2 and scope correction; red-before grid crash and early-abort probes |

| KQ30 | A reusable identity helper refuses I/O failures at its own boundary, before returning a comparison result; the fixed finite injected population separately records null returns, partial digests and explicit refusals, proves each fault reached its target, preserves successful digest bytes and intentional exclusions, and retains non-OSError propagation controls. The helper's outcome and a caller's later backstop are reported separately. | An error silently becomes a smaller identity; an os.access precheck replaces actual error handling; root-dependent chmod alone supplies failure evidence; a caller's existing refusal is claimed as a new producer-level improvement; an untriggered injection or arbitrary crash earns refusal credit. | `lessons/round-22.md` M1; R21 KQ29 protected the producer but left the bare install_tree contract weaker |

| KQ32 | A report-landing audit is explicitly limited to the trusted fleet/lane repositories until repository-local Git-config/history and UTF-8/error hardening is demonstrated separately. | Global/system config and environment scrubbing is treated as suppressing local Git configuration or as a security guarantee for arbitrary repositories. | `lessons/round-22.md` D4; CloseKama21 rounds[406] and late C1EnvSentinel debt |

| KQ33 (qualifies KQ28's report-wide full-hash rule only) | A 40-hex occurrence is classified as an external source reference only inside an exact first HTTPS source URL (or its source-census-normalized form) from a structurally valid Registry row in the committed SOURCES blob, outside Landed changes. Bare copies, unregistered/superset URLs, malformed rows, Leads and worktree-only registrations remain checked; Landed resolution/omission rules never change. | All occurrences of a hash are exempted by value; a generic URL or substring hides a bad citation; committed-source loading errors become a clean/missing fallback; classification is called source-validity or untrusted-repository proof. | `lessons/round-22.md` M4; pinned census-report red/green witness and source-URL boundary selftests |

| KQ34 (narrows, does not supersede, KQ32) | A gate's isolation or exit-class promise is credited only through a committed crosswalk that is not self-selecting: every repository-local channel the promise names, and every channel a probe shows violating it, has a fault row with an established premise (a failed premise is could-not-evaluate), a frozen-arm observation on the same pinned population that crashes, flips, hangs or executes, and a current-arm expectation of exit and defect kinds with a pinned reason string for every exit-2 refusal, or the channel is reported open; every isolation element has a single-element mutant whose reported failed rows are pasted, kill credit goes to a channel only when that channel's row fails with the fault the row names, and control-only or blanket-parse kills are reported as shared-protocol; an element is defensive-only only when a fault row aimed at its channel passes without it because a named dominating refusal runs first. Population and auditor digests are pinned, unfaulted controls are met on the same population, and every quoted count names the measured revision. | A docstring or report says audited repositories "cannot be redirected", "run no repository-configured program", "errors are never verdicts" or "hardened" beyond the crosswalk; a promise channel has no mutant (the NUL `-z`/`%x00` log-record element at `245a37f`); any nonzero grid exit, an unrelated row, or an unreported control-only/blanket-parse failure earns a kill; defensive-only is assigned by survival alone (at `245a37f` a `remote.<n>.partialclonefilter` promisor remote lazy-fetches and runs `core.sshCommand` once `--no-lazy-fetch` is removed); a refusal is counted without its pinned reason; a fixture whose fault was never established is counted, or a uniform `require()` is claimed where builders only construct; counts are quoted without their population digest; open rows (alternates, gitfile redirect) are omitted, or KQ32's trusted-repository-only use is lifted. | `lessons/round-23.md` M1/M2; `tests/report-audit/repo-state-grid.py`; `tests/report-audit/isolation-mutants.py`; `falsify/advice/CritDefensiveOnly.md` |
